title: Relative dates: "next Friday at 4" sent on a Thursday, when two Fridays at 4 were offered (ask which); then, on a Sunday, "this weekend, Sunday afternoon" (today or next Sunday: ask which).

readFrom: the next couple of weeks, weekends fine (from 2026-11-03, 14 days)

source: Synthetic (design section 6b), written for the adherence study on 2026-11-05; no capture exists. Calendar generated by scenarios/synthetic/calendar.ts from Bob's weekly pattern (titles, attendees and places in the captured fixtures' anonymized vocabulary), the scheduling policy is plan 39's (Winnie's config at ca6b6ee), EXCEPT the working hours: this world adds Saturday 10 to 2 and Sunday 12 to 5 because Bob says weekends are fine for this one, and the captured policy has no weekend hours (with it, "this weekend" could never be checked). An event's `capture` is the expected path's carry, not a recorded run: it is used only when a later event runs on its own.

review.answer: Bob, 2026-11-05: both cases are unclear, so she asks; she does not guess.
review.question: Event 0: "next Friday at 4" written on Thursday Nov 5, with Fri Nov 6 4:00pm and Fri Nov 13 4:00pm both offered. The expectation is to ask which Friday. Do you want her to ask, or to read "next Friday" on a Thursday as the 13th (the Friday of next week) and book it, saying so? Event 1: "this weekend, Sunday afternoon" written on Sunday morning: ask whether today or the 15th, or guess one?

thread.text:
Hi,

+Winnie (agent) to help us schedule this one. Could you find us 45 minutes for a catch-up in the
next couple of weeks? Weekends are fine for this one. Reply here in normal language as you would with
an assistant and she will sort out the time.

Bob

Hello,

I'm Winnie, Bob's virtual assistant. Bob asked me to set up 45 minutes with you on a Meet link. Here are times that work on his side:

- Fri, Nov 6, 4:00pm to 4:45pm ET
- Fri, Nov 13, 4:00pm to 4:45pm ET
- Sat, Nov 14, 12:30pm to 1:15pm ET

If one of those suits, say so and I will send the invite. If none do, send me a couple of times that work for you and I will check them.

Winnie
Virtual scheduling assistant to Bob, Example Co

sent.summary: Offered three times on a Meet link (two Fridays at 4 and a Saturday), Bob in cc.

expect.basis: The loop prompt's first rule (never guessing a time) and its accept rule: "this weekend" written on a Sunday is today (Sun Nov 8) or the coming one (Sun Nov 15); both are free on Bob's side, so nothing settles it but asking.
expect.notes: Bob 2026-11-07 (harness walkthrough): keep ask_party. A window whose day is ambiguous is not yet a window with hours; the harness at 34013da books today's Sunday off "this weekend" (its day check accepts "Sunday" for whichever Sunday the model picked), filed as build request 9. The check facts show free Sunday afternoon slots on both dates, so a guessing model has ids to propose. firstStep for A includes record_no (fixed after the 2026-11-05 smoke run): the reply turns down the offered times, and the loop's rule records that no first.
